in_text_mentions: In Figure 2, the MRI scan shows several poorly limited pseudonodular hepatic lesions, some of which are confluent, with subcapsular localization, hypointense on T1, and hyperintense on T2 with peripheral enhancement in portal phase. Some lesions presented a serpiginous pattern. These findings were suggestive of infectious etiology and small liver abscesses. There was also slight dilation of the small bile ducts in segments VI and VII and peri-aortic, celiac, and portal adenopathies of likely reactive nature, with a maximum diameter of 14 mm. There were no signs of malignant disease.

in_text_mentions: A 52-year-old woman who had previously traveled to a developing country was admitted to our emergency department with fever, colicky abdominal pain, and pruritus. Laboratory tests showed hypereosinophilia (1432 eosinophils/µL, limit value <500) and direct hyperbilirubinemia (2.5 mg/dL, reference range 0–1.3 mg/dL). Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography revealed endoluminal filling defects into a dilated common bile duct (CBD) and in the gallbladder ( Fig. 1 ). Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) was then planned to treat choledocholithiasis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial T2 MRI panel A shows T2-hyperintense parasitic liver lesion attributed to Fasciola hepatica infection confirmed serologically; article title and caption attribute lesion and associated thrombosis/perfusion change to fascioliasis. B: Post-contrast T1 panel B shows same segment VI parasitic lesion with minimal enhancement plus focal portal vein thrombosis and perfusion alteration, captioned as fascioliasis manifestation. C: T2 panel C shows localized bile duct dilation in segment VII (white arrows) indicating ductal phase of Fasciola hepatica infection per caption and serologically confirmed fascioliasis article. D: Post-contrast T1 panel D shows localized bile duct dilation in segment VII captioned as associated with ductal phase of fascioliasis in confirmed Fasciola hepatica case.
